    "For Path Efficiency: Test H0: mu_Combined = mu_ICMS = mu_Dim = mu_Bright = mu_Sham against H1: at least one mean differs.",
    "For Average Speed: Test H0: mu_Combined = mu_ICMS = mu_Dim = mu_Bright = mu_Sham against H1: at least one mean differs.",

  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence of observations: Verify that trials are independent within and across mice; check for repeated measures structure if multiple trials per mouse exist.",
    "Normality of residuals: Inspect Q-Q plots and histograms of residuals for each ANOVA model; apply log or square root transformations if severe skewness is detected (especially for Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency given their wide ranges).",
    "Homogeneity of variances (Homoscedasticity): Conduct Levene's test or Bartlett's test for equal variances across the five paradigm groups.",
    "Outlier detection: Identify extreme values in Time-to-Target (max 201.39 vs mean 2.80) and Path Efficiency (max 29.82 vs mean 0.47) that may violate normality assumptions.",
    "For Success variable: Verify expected cell counts are sufficient (>5) for Chi-Square test or use exact tests if sparse."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus ANOVA F-test is significant for a given metric, proceed with post-hoc pairwise comparisons.",
    "Use Tukey's HSD (Honestly Significant Difference) test for all pairwise comparisons to control the family-wise error rate.",
    "Report effect sizes (e.g., eta-squared) for significant differences.",
    "For Success (Chi-Square): Use post-hoc pairwise comparisons with Bonferroni correction or Fisher's Exact Test for specific group comparisons if needed."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Time-to-Target: Likely significant differences; ICMS Only or Dim Visual Only may show slower times compared to Combined or Sham due to sensory deprivation or noise.",
    "Success: Likely significant differences; Combined stimulation may yield higher success rates than Sham or single-modality conditions.",
    "Path Efficiency: Likely significant differences; Combined or Sham conditions may show more direct paths compared to ICMS Only.",
    "Average Speed: Likely significant differences; conditions with sensory input (Combined, Visual) may support higher speeds than ICMS Only.",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion): Likely significant differences; Combined or Sham may show lower dispersion (more consistent heading) compared to ICMS Only."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Success variable is binary, violating ANOVA assumptions; requires alternative non-parametric or generalized linear modeling approaches.",
    "Skewed distributions in Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency (high max/min ratios) may require transformation or non-parametric alternatives (e.g., Kruskal-Wallis).",
    "Potential violation of independence if multiple trials per mouse are not accounted for (repeated measures).",
    "Unbalanced sample sizes across paradigms (e.g., Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505) may affect power and homogeneity of variance tests.",
    "No information provided on mouse-level random effects; treating data as purely independent ignores potential inter-subject variability."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct a mixed-effects model (GLMM) for each response variable, treating 'Mouse' as a random intercept to account for repeated measures, and use appropriate link functions (e.g., logit for Success, identity or log for continuous variables) to handle distributional assumptions."
}
